answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The ivory multiplier is published, charged in quartz, and jade lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2641 identities would post 4569 proofs and burn roughly 40 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
